name: Article
description: Read the current revision of a Wikipedia (or sister-project) article by exact title: full wikitext (or HTML with body), abstract, categories, redirects, connected Wikidata QID, license, and revision credibility signals. Use structured-contents instead when you want infobox fields, sections or references already parsed. From https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin pass name `Berlin` and project `dewiki`. Not a search: titles must match exactly.

options.name: name
options.about: Exact article title as on the wiki, for example `Marie_Curie` or `Marie Curie`. Case-sensitive: Wikipedia titles start with a capital letter. From a URL such as https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_Curie, use the part after /wiki/.

options.name: project
options.about: Wikimedia project identifier: language code plus project code, for example `enwiki` (English Wikipedia), `frwiki`, `dewiki`, `enwiktionary` or `eswikivoyage`. Defaults to `enwiki` when neither project nor language is given. `reference/projects` lists every identifier.

options.name: language
options.about: Wikimedia language code, for example `en`, `fr` or `zh-yue`. Returns the article from any project in that language; combine with project to pin one wiki.

options.name: fields
options.about: Return only these fields, in dot notation, for example `name`, `abstract`, `url`, `version.identifier`. Omit for the full record. Wikimedia returns exactly the fields named.

options.name: limit
options.about: Most matching articles to return, 1 to 10. More than one only helps when no project is pinned and the title exists on several wikis.

options.name: body
options.about: Which article_body format to include when fields is not given: `wikitext` (default, compact), `html` (MediaWiki DOM, often 5-10x larger), `both`, or `none` for metadata and abstract only.

name: Structured article
description: Read a Wikipedia article pre-parsed into JSON: one-line description, abstract, infobox fields, sections as paragraphs and lists with links, references and tables. Best for extracting facts such as a person's birth date or a city's population without parsing HTML. Beta upstream, with the most complete coverage on en, de, fr, es, pt, it, nl, cy and id Wikipedia. Exact title, as for articles/lookup.
